title: Project tracker
summary: Build your first Effect feature: create, find, edit, and archive learning projects.
outcome: A usable local project tracker with validated writes, recoverable forms, and tests against replaceable storage.
prerequisites: React forms, TypeScript unions, and async functions. Start here before the other projects.
model: Project: id, name (1–100 trimmed characters), goal, status (active or archived), createdAt, updatedAt.
Generate identity once per create attempt. Define whether archived names may be reused before adding uniqueness rules.
Follow src/db/schema.ts and src/db/repos/ for persistence conventions; add a versioned Dexie migration for a new table.
boundaries: React form → createProject operation → ProjectRepository → Dexie. Keep validation in the operation and run the Effect at the UI boundary.

milestones.title: Create and list projects
milestones.brief: Ship one complete path from a project form to durable storage and back to the list.
milestones.explanation: Effect<Success, Error, Requirements> describes a computation, its expected failures, and its dependencies. Building an Effect does not execute the write. Decode unknown form input with Schema, compose the operation with Effect.gen, then execute it at the boundary. Invalid input must stop before storage is called.
steps: Write examples for a valid name, whitespace-only name, overlong name, and a storage failure. Trim before validating length.
Add the project model, migration, repository, create operation, and labeled form. Show loading, empty, success, and error states; preserve the draft after failure.
Wrap the Dexie promise boundary with Effect.tryPromise and map failures into an explicit storage error. Disable repeated submit while pending and inspect the actual saved records.

checks.label: A valid project appears once and survives reload.
Blank and overlong names produce useful errors and no database writes.
A rejected save preserves the draft and can be retried successfully.

milestones.experiment: Make the repository reject the first save. Submit the same draft twice, then restore storage and retry. Predict the record count before inspecting it.
milestones.review: Trace input normalization, validation, persistence, and rendering. Avoid calling runPromise inside the repository; the UI boundary owns execution and presentation of failures.
milestones.stretch: Add a stable operation ID so an ambiguous response can be retried without a duplicate project.

milestones.title: Edit, search, and archive
milestones.brief: Complete the tracker with editing, active/archive filters, and recovery from missing records.
milestones.explanation: A missing project and a failed database connection need different responses. Represent expected domain failures explicitly, then map them to useful UI states. Archiving is a reversible update; define its behavior separately from permanent deletion.
steps: Specify case-insensitive search, active/archive filtering, and the behavior of an editor opened for a missing project.
Implement update, archive, and restore operations. Reuse the name validation and preserve identity and createdAt during edits.
Add a keyboard-accessible editor and archive confirmation. Clear a search with no matches; verify the full list returns.

checks.label: Edits persist without changing identity or creation time.
Search and status filters compose, including an empty result.
Archive and restore survive reload; a missing record has a recoverable state.

milestones.experiment: Open the editor, remove its record from a test store, then save. The app must not silently recreate the record or report success.
milestones.review: Check that the write boundary enforces the same rules as the form. A disabled button alone cannot enforce a business rule.
milestones.stretch: Add a revision field and reject an edit when another tab has already changed the project.

milestones.title: Replace storage in tests
milestones.brief: Give the same project operations a Dexie implementation and a deterministic in-memory test implementation.
milestones.explanation: A service defines what an operation needs; a Layer supplies that dependency. The business operation should not need to know which implementation it receives. A fake repository is useful for controlled failures, but it does not prove Dexie migrations or transactions work.
steps: Define ProjectRepository with the smallest interface needed by create, list, update, and archive. Keep storage-specific types inside the adapter.
Provide live and in-memory Layers. Supply a controllable ID generator and clock where assertions depend on identity or timestamps.
Run behavior checks against the in-memory service and persistence checks against Dexie. Document where the application constructs and disposes its runtime.

checks.label: Business operations run with either repository without changing their code.
Tests cover missing records and storage failures without a live backend.
A Dexie integration check proves reload persistence and the migration path.

milestones.experiment: Replace the clock and ID generator with fixed values. Run the same create case twice in fresh stores and compare the entire result.
milestones.review: Explain each type parameter in one operation and which Layer satisfies its requirements. Keep test state isolated between cases.
milestones.stretch: Write a second adapter using a local HTTP API and run a shared repository contract against both implementations.

milestones.title: Make forms usable without a mouse
milestones.brief: Turn field errors and asynchronous saves into a keyboard-accessible experience that preserves the user's place and input.
milestones.explanation: A typed error becomes useful only when a person can recover from it. Distinguish field validation from a form-wide storage failure. Associate messages with their inputs, move focus deliberately after a failed submit, and announce save results without interrupting typing. Loading, disabled, and read-only mean different things; choose each according to the interaction.
steps: Draw the focus sequence for opening, submitting, correcting, and closing the editor. Include the empty-name and failed-storage paths.
Map validation errors to labeled fields, connect descriptions, and add a concise live status. Keep the last entered values after a rejected write.
Run the flow with only Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, and Escape. Inspect accessible names and verify that closing returns focus to the original trigger.

checks.label: Every field and error has an accessible relationship.
Keyboard users can finish and recover without a focus trap.
A failed save retains values and announces a useful next action.

milestones.experiment: Submit two invalid fields, correct only the first, then submit again. Check that focus reaches the remaining problem and that stale error text disappears.
milestones.review: Ask the agent to justify each focus move and status announcement. A screenshot cannot establish keyboard behavior; include the sequence you actually performed.
milestones.stretch: Test at 200% zoom with a long translated error message and document the layout changes required.

milestones.title: Archive selected projects safely
milestones.brief: Add row selection and bulk archive with an explicit contract for partial failure, changing filters, and repeated requests.
milestones.explanation: Selection is a set of stable identities, not the current row positions. Decide whether a bulk action is atomic or returns per-item results before designing its UI. If filters change, a hidden selected row must not become a surprise write. Effect can orchestrate a batch, but the repository still owns transactional guarantees.
steps: Specify what select-all means: visible page, filtered result, or entire database. Display the count and scope before confirmation.
Implement the chosen transaction or per-item result contract. Validate missing and already archived rows, and prevent duplicate command submission.
Test a selection across two pages, a filter change, and one row disappearing before confirmation. Verify exact affected IDs rather than just counts.

checks.label: The confirmation accurately describes every targeted row.
Failure behavior matches the advertised atomic or partial policy.
Repeated submission does not corrupt selection or stored status.

milestones.experiment: Select three records, hide one with a filter, then archive. Compare the actual targets with the confirmation text and your declared selection policy.
milestones.review: Review the command payload independently of the rendered table. Avoid deriving the write list from whatever happens to be visible when a promise resolves.
milestones.stretch: Add an undo receipt that restores only rows still matching the revision created by this bulk action.

milestones.title: Upgrade existing local databases
milestones.brief: Add a project priority field while preserving installations created before the field existed, including archived projects and personal edits.
milestones.explanation: Fresh-install tests miss upgrade failures. A migration needs a real old-shape fixture, a deterministic default, and a rule for partially populated data. Data defaults belong at the schema boundary, while form defaults are presentation choices. Opening the database twice must not apply a destructive transformation twice.
steps: Capture a versioned old database fixture containing active and archived records. Write the expected transformed shape before touching the migration.
Add the field with a validated default and a versioned Dexie upgrade. Preserve identities, timestamps with historical meaning, and existing user-entered text.
Open the old fixture with the new build, reopen it again, and exercise create/edit/archive. Compare records and verify old JSON imports have an explicit defaulting policy.

checks.label: Old records remain readable and editable after upgrade.
Reopening an upgraded store does not repeat or duplicate migration work.
Malformed priority values are rejected at the write boundary.

milestones.experiment: Put an invalid legacy value in one record and interrupt the upgrade in a disposable profile. Describe whether the transaction rolls back and how startup communicates recovery.
milestones.review: Record both fresh installation and upgrade evidence. Never use a full database reset as a production migration strategy for someone else's saved learning work.
milestones.stretch: Rehearse an additive migration that allows the previous application version to keep reading the new records.

milestones.title: Normalize before measuring
milestones.brief: Submit a project named with 99 letters surrounded by three spaces on each side.
milestones.explanation: The stored name and the name whose length was validated must be the same normalized value.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Submit a project named with 99 letters surrounded by three spaces on each side. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Move trimming into the shared decode operation before the length constraint.
Test 99 letters, 100 letters, 101 letters, and whitespace-only input. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The first two names save without surrounding spaces.
Overlong and empty normalized names never reach the repository.
Recovery evidence: Make the form bypass its client validation and submit 101 letters directly. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Make the form bypass its client validation and submit 101 letters directly.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the operation independently enforce the constraint when React is absent?
milestones.stretch: Add an explicit policy for Unicode grapheme counts and document its tradeoff.

milestones.title: Preserve a rejected draft
milestones.brief: Enter a long project goal, then make the first repository write reject with a quota error.
milestones.explanation: A failed durable write must not consume the draft or claim that a project exists.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Enter a long project goal, then make the first repository write reject with a quota error. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Map quota failure to a recoverable form state with retained name and goal.
Retry after restoring capacity and inspect the saved identity and goal. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The retry stores exactly the text visible in the recovered editor.
The failed attempt produces no success toast or empty replacement form.
Recovery evidence: Reject twice before permitting a third write to finish. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Reject twice before permitting a third write to finish.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Can an error handler accidentally clear the draft through a finally callback?
milestones.stretch: Provide a copy-draft action when storage remains unavailable for several attempts.

milestones.title: Separate empty from loading
milestones.brief: Open a clean database through a repository whose initial list takes two seconds.
milestones.explanation: An unresolved read does not establish that the user's project collection is empty.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Open a clean database through a repository whose initial list takes two seconds. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Represent pending, successful empty, successful populated, and failed reads explicitly.
Hold the read promise and inspect visible text before resolving an empty result. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The empty-state create action appears after successful resolution.
A failed list is never presented as a confirmed empty collection.
Recovery evidence: Reject the delayed read after the user opens the create form. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Reject the delayed read after the user opens the create form.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does refresh overwrite a draft because collection state and editor state share a reducer?
milestones.stretch: Add a quiet refresh indicator that retains previously confirmed rows.

milestones.title: Defeat double submission
milestones.brief: Press Enter twice quickly while creating a project called Billing redesign on a slow disk.
milestones.explanation: One user creation attempt owns one stable identity across repeated delivery.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Press Enter twice quickly while creating a project called Billing redesign on a slow disk. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Generate the command ID before execution and guard pending submission at the boundary.
Deliver the same operation twice against the repository with completion ordering reversed. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Exactly one project and one success announcement exist afterward.
A second intentional creation after completion receives a different identity.
Recovery evidence: Resolve the second callback before the first callback and observe the form. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Resolve the second callback before the first callback and observe the form.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Is duplicate protection enforced below the button rather than only through disabled styling?
milestones.stretch: Persist pending operation identities so reload after an ambiguous write is safe.

milestones.title: Keep time deterministic
milestones.brief: Create two projects with a clock frozen at 2030-01-02T03:04:05Z and known generated IDs.
milestones.explanation: Creation timestamps are domain inputs that must be reproducible independently of wall-clock scheduling.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Create two projects with a clock frozen at 2030-01-02T03:04:05Z and known generated IDs. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Inject the clock and ID service into the create operation.
Use fixed services in a test and compare the entire stored rows. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Both rows receive the specified timestamp and distinct expected IDs.
A clock failure produces no partially initialized persisted project.
Recovery evidence: Change the clock between constructing and executing an Effect and predict the recorded time. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Change the clock between constructing and executing an Effect and predict the recorded time.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Is time read at execution, and is the intended timing documented?
milestones.stretch: Add monotonic revision numbers without pretending wall-clock timestamps are unique.

milestones.title: Map unknown rejections
milestones.brief: Make a legacy repository reject with a string, then an Error, then an arbitrary object.
milestones.explanation: An external rejection has unknown shape until the adapter maps it into a safe typed failure.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Make a legacy repository reject with a string, then an Error, then an arbitrary object. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Wrap the promise boundary and preserve useful diagnostic causes without exposing them in the form.
Exercise all three rejection shapes with the same create operation. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Each failure becomes the documented storage-error variant.
Raw object serialization and stack traces do not appear in the user message.
Recovery evidence: Throw an object containing a circular reference to challenge naive error formatting. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Throw an object containing a circular reference to challenge naive error formatting.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the adapter catch only external promise failure without hiding programming defects?
milestones.stretch: Introduce a diagnostic correlation ID that links the safe message to local logs.

milestones.title: Choose a duplicate-name policy
milestones.brief: Seed active Atlas and archived Atlas projects, then create atlas with surrounding whitespace.
milestones.explanation: Name uniqueness is a product rule with an explicit comparison and archive scope.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Seed active Atlas and archived Atlas projects, then create atlas with surrounding whitespace. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Specify case folding and active-versus-all scope before adding a repository constraint.
Race two creates whose names become equal after normalization. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The accepted rows match the written duplicate-name policy.
The losing operation receives a useful conflict rather than a generic disk error.
Recovery evidence: Restore the archived Atlas while another active Atlas exists. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Restore the archived Atlas while another active Atlas exists.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Are create, rename, and restore all checked against the same uniqueness rule?
milestones.stretch: Test a locale-sensitive name and document whether comparison uses locale or stable normalization.

milestones.title: Cancel without imaginary rollback
milestones.brief: Start a delayed project save, close the editor, and reopen the project list before completion.
milestones.explanation: Closing a UI does not prove that a durable operation was rolled back.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Start a delayed project save, close the editor, and reopen the project list before completion. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Define whether saving continues or is cancellable and present that behavior honestly.
Complete the write after the editor unmounts and inspect durable data and announcements. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The eventual row is represented consistently after the next list read.
No obsolete callback reopens the closed editor or steals focus.
Recovery evidence: Interrupt while the storage adapter has already accepted the write. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Interrupt while the storage adapter has already accepted the write.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does cleanup distinguish stopping observation from reversing persistence?
milestones.stretch: Add an operation-status lookup for ambiguous completion after navigation.

milestones.title: Keep form text inert
milestones.brief: Create a project with a goal containing an HTML image tag and a script-looking URL.
milestones.explanation: User-authored text remains data unless a separately validated rendering feature explicitly interprets it.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Create a project with a goal containing an HTML image tag and a script-looking URL. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Render plain text and inspect any preview or highlighting path for unsafe markup insertion.
Reload the record and inspect the DOM and attempted network requests. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The complete literal goal remains readable as text.
No element or request is created from embedded markup.
Recovery evidence: Paste the same payload into the search field and empty-state message. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Paste the same payload into the search field and empty-state message.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Did an agent add innerHTML merely to highlight matching words?
milestones.stretch: Implement highlight spans through escaped text segments and test mixed Unicode input.

milestones.title: Reject stale editor revisions
milestones.brief: Open revision 4 of Atlas in two tabs and save different goals from each.
milestones.explanation: A save based on old state must not silently replace a newer accepted edit.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Open revision 4 of Atlas in two tabs and save different goals from each. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Require the expected revision in the update command and compare atomically in storage.
Save tab A, then tab B, and inspect the persisted revision and goal. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Tab A advances the revision exactly once.
Tab B receives a conflict with its unsaved goal still available.
Recovery evidence: Refresh the conflicting record while retaining the stale draft for comparison. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Refresh the conflicting record while retaining the stale draft for comparison.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Can the conflict path distinguish a deleted row from an updated row?
milestones.stretch: Add a field-level comparison view that lets the user compose a fresh revision.

milestones.title: Search literal punctuation
milestones.brief: Seed projects named C++, foo.bar, and roadmap[2026], then search punctuation fragments.
milestones.explanation: A simple substring search must not accidentally interpret user text as a regular expression.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Seed projects named C++, foo.bar, and roadmap[2026], then search punctuation fragments. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Implement normalized literal matching and preserve the original display strings.
Search ++, ., [, and a whitespace-only query under both archive filters. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Only names containing the requested literal fragment match.
Malformed regex-like text never crashes or widens the search unexpectedly.
Recovery evidence: Paste a very long sequence of parentheses into the query. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Paste a very long sequence of parentheses into the query.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the code require regex at all, and if so is every metacharacter escaped?
milestones.stretch: Add indexed prefix matching and document how its semantics differ from substring search.

milestones.title: Archive during editing
milestones.brief: Edit an active project in one view while another view archives that same record.
milestones.explanation: An edit must respect the current lifecycle state rather than restoring stale active status.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Edit an active project in one view while another view archives that same record. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Limit editable fields and handle the archived transition explicitly in the command.
Save the old form after the archive operation commits. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The archive state remains durable after the attempted edit.
A stale form never reactivates the record by spreading old properties.
Recovery evidence: Restore the record and retry with a fresh revision. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Restore the record and retry with a fresh revision.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does update accept an explicit patch instead of a whole stale entity snapshot?
milestones.stretch: Offer a deliberate restore-and-edit command with its own confirmation.

milestones.title: Navigate away from dirty input
milestones.brief: Change a project goal, then use a sidebar link before saving.
milestones.explanation: Unsaved text must have a predictable lifetime across route changes and cancellation.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Change a project goal, then use a sidebar link before saving. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Choose a route-leave confirmation or local draft policy and implement it consistently.
Exercise save, discard, stay, browser Back, and a same-record link. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Choosing stay preserves the exact draft and focused field.
Choosing discard never creates an unrequested write.
Recovery evidence: Fail a save that was initiated from the leave confirmation. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Fail a save that was initiated from the leave confirmation.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does a failed transition keep both the draft and the intended destination understandable?
milestones.stretch: Restore a local draft after browser restart with a visible age indicator.

milestones.title: Missing record recovery
milestones.brief: Open an edit URL for a project removed from the test database.
milestones.explanation: Absence is a normal domain result and must not fall through into accidental creation.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Open an edit URL for a project removed from the test database. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Return a typed missing-project result with a link back to a usable list.
Delete the row after initial read but before update and submit once. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The interface explains that the project is unavailable.
The update never inserts a replacement with the missing ID.
Recovery evidence: Make the list read fail after the missing-record message appears. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Make the list read fail after the missing-record message appears.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Are not-found and storage-unavailable presented as different recovery choices?
milestones.stretch: Preserve the unsaved text in a copyable panel on the missing-record page.

milestones.title: Make clear search predictable
milestones.brief: Open an archived-only list with query alpha, then clear the search field.
milestones.explanation: Clearing one filter must leave unrelated filter state and navigation history coherent.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Open an archived-only list with query alpha, then clear the search field. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Represent search and lifecycle filter separately in the URL or state model.
Clear via button, keyboard deletion, and browser Back after changing the query. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Clearing restores all archived projects and keeps the archive filter.
The action does not silently switch to active projects or another project.
Recovery evidence: Reload after clearing and compare the resulting visible collection. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Reload after clearing and compare the resulting visible collection.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does one state reset helper accidentally erase filters it does not own?
milestones.stretch: Support shareable search links while excluding private draft text from URLs.

milestones.title: Distinguish patch from replacement
milestones.brief: A stored project has name, goal, priority, and a migration-added color; rename only its name.
milestones.explanation: A narrow edit preserves fields that its editor does not own.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: A stored project has name, goal, priority, and a migration-added color; rename only its name. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Define a validated update patch and apply only allowed keys inside the repository.
Rename using an older client payload that does not know the color field. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The new name persists while goal, priority, and color remain unchanged.
Unknown or immutable patch keys are rejected according to the contract.
Recovery evidence: Send createdAt and id in a malicious update patch. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Send createdAt and id in a malicious update patch.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Did the agent use object spreading where an explicit allowed-field mapping is needed?
milestones.stretch: Add contract fixtures for older clients that omit newly introduced optional fields.

milestones.title: Sort without losing identity
milestones.brief: Create three projects with equal updatedAt values and edit the second while sorting the table.
milestones.explanation: Rendered row identity must survive ordering changes even when sort keys tie.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Create three projects with equal updatedAt values and edit the second while sorting the table. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Use stable IDs for React keys and add a deterministic ID tiebreaker to ordering.
Change the sort while one row contains an open inline editor. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The editor stays attached to the same project ID.
Text, errors, and pending indicators never jump into a neighboring row.
Recovery evidence: Update another row so it crosses the edited row in sort order. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Update another row so it crosses the edited row in sort order.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Are array indices used anywhere as identity for mutable rows?
milestones.stretch: Preserve the edited row in view using explicit scroll behavior instead of index guesses.

milestones.title: Undo only your archive
milestones.brief: Archive revision 8, then let another tab restore and rename the project before pressing Undo.
milestones.explanation: An undo receipt may reverse its own unchanged result but must not overwrite later work.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Archive revision 8, then let another tab restore and rename the project before pressing Undo. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Capture the produced revision and require it for conditional undo.
Perform archive, external rename, then undo with the original receipt. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Later edits remain intact and the receipt reports its conflict.
Undo never restores a whole pre-archive snapshot over new fields.
Recovery evidence: Press the same undo action twice after one successful restoration. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Press the same undo action twice after one successful restoration.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does compensation target one transition or pretend to rewind the database?
milestones.stretch: Add receipt expiry and explain why an expired receipt cannot promise safe reversal.

milestones.title: Specify repository ordering
milestones.brief: Seed three project rows in different insertion orders in memory and Dexie adapters.
milestones.explanation: The repository contract must define whether ordering is guaranteed or delegated to its caller.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Seed three project rows in different insertion orders in memory and Dexie adapters. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Write a contract fixture with equal timestamps and a deterministic expected ordering.
Run the same read assertion against both adapters without adapting expected results. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Both implementations return the documented ordering.
The fake cannot pass by relying on an insertion-order accident.
Recovery evidence: Reverse seed order and repeat the contract suite. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Reverse seed order and repeat the contract suite.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the service signature make its ordering promise visible to callers?
milestones.stretch: Add pagination contract checks that prove stable boundaries with equal sort keys.

milestones.title: Remove shared fake state
milestones.brief: Run two independent project-operation tests that each create an item named Scratch.
milestones.explanation: A fresh test service must not inherit records or failure switches from another test.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Run two independent project-operation tests that each create an item named Scratch. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Allocate fake state inside each Layer construction rather than module-level mutable storage.
Run the tests in reversed order and with overlapping execution. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Each test observes only its own Scratch project.
A rejected-write flag in one fixture never leaks into another fixture.
Recovery evidence: Mutate one fake after both runtimes are constructed. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Mutate one fake after both runtimes are constructed.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Are default maps or arrays reused through a singleton export?
milestones.stretch: Expose a read-only inspection capability for tests without exposing mutable production internals.

milestones.title: Model failure before mutation
milestones.brief: Configure the in-memory repository to fail the next create of project Delta.
milestones.explanation: A failed write should match the live adapter's atomicity, including whether data changed.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Configure the in-memory repository to fail the next create of project Delta. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Place the injected failure at the same semantic boundary as the live operation.
After failure, list rows and retry the same command ID. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The fake and live adapter agree on durable state after rejection.
The test fake never inserts a row before reporting a precommit failure.
Recovery evidence: Add a separate ambiguous-after-commit failure fixture and compare outcomes. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Add a separate ambiguous-after-commit failure fixture and compare outcomes.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does one generic failure switch collapse materially different storage behaviors?
milestones.stretch: Document failure injection points with before-commit and after-commit names.

milestones.title: Keep execution at the edge
milestones.brief: Trace createProject from React through validation and repository insertion.
milestones.explanation: An operation remains composable when it describes work without secretly starting another runtime.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Trace createProject from React through validation and repository insertion. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
